resumen: Personas y estudios: relatives = parientes (parents = papá y mamá), degree = carrera universitaria (career = trayectoria profesional), library = biblioteca (librería = bookshop), lecture = clase magistral o charla (lectura = reading).
Verbos falsos amigos: attend = asistir a (assist = ayudar), intend = pretender (pretend = fingir), carry out = realizar (realise = darse cuenta), summarise = resumir (resume = reanudar).

Adjetivos y adverbios: actually = en realidad (actualmente = currently), eventually = al final, sensible = sensato (sensible = sensitive), sympathetic = comprensivo (simpático = friendly), embarrassed = avergonzado (embarazada = pregnant), large = grande (largo = long).
Sustantivos: carpet = alfombra (carpeta = folder), success = éxito (exit = salida), argument = discusión (el argumento de una historia = the plot), casualties = víctimas (casualidad = chance).
Say / tell, remind / remember, borrow / lend: tell someone something, say something (to someone); Remind me to call her (otra persona te hace recordar); borrow from (recibir), lend to (dar).
Rise / raise, affect / effect, rob / steal: Prices rise, pero They raise prices; affect es el verbo y effect el sustantivo (have an effect on); rob a bank, steal money.
Lose / miss / waste, win / earn, job / work: lose your keys, miss the bus, waste time; win a prize, earn a salary; a job es contable y work incontable.

Trip / travel / journey, bring / take, fun / funny, economic / economical, advice / advise: a journey o a trip, pero travel en general; bring hacia aquí, take hacia allá; fun = divertido, funny = gracioso; an economical car gasta poco; advice es el sustantivo y advise el verbo.

preguntas.q: Everyone thinks Tom is Scottish, but he's ___ from Wales.
preguntas.x: Actually significa «en realidad»: corrige una idea equivocada. «Actualmente» se dice currently o nowadays, que aquí no tienen sentido porque el lugar de origen no cambia; actual es un adjetivo («real, verdadero»).

preguntas.q: I left my ___ with all my notes on a desk in the university ___ where I was studying.
preguntas.x: «Carpeta» es folder (o file); carpet es una alfombra. «Biblioteca» es library, mientras que la «librería» es a bookshop, donde se compran libros y no se estudia.

preguntas.q: My sister is ___; the baby is due in March.
preguntas.x: «Embarazada» es pregnant. Embarrassed es un falso amigo que significa «avergonzado, apenado» (I was so embarrassed!), y pregnancy es el sustantivo («embarazo»).

preguntas.q: If we don't leave now, we'll ___ the beginning of the film.
preguntas.x: «Perderse» algo que ocurre (un tren, una clase, el inicio de una película) es miss. Lose es perder un objeto o un partido (lose your keys), waste es desperdiciar (waste time) y loose es un adjetivo («flojo, suelto»).

preguntas.q: The trip to the science museum was really ___; we learnt a lot and had a great time.
preguntas.x: Fun significa «divertido, entretenido» (algo que se disfruta); funny es «gracioso», algo que da risa (a funny joke). Fan es un aficionado y funnily es un adverbio.

preguntas.q: My brother has finally found a ___; he ___ about £1,800 a month.
preguntas.x: Job es un empleo concreto y es contable (a job); work es incontable, así que a work no se dice. Un sueldo se earn; win es ganar un premio, un sorteo o un partido.

preguntas.q: Be careful what you say about his essay; he's very ___ to criticism.
preguntas.x: Sensitive significa «sensible, susceptible» (sensitive to criticism, sensitive skin). Sensible es un falso amigo que significa «sensato» (a sensible decision); sensitivity es el sustantivo y sensibly el adverbio.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “My aunts, uncles and cousins went to Professor Ruiz's talk.”
preguntas.a: My relatives attended Professor Ruiz's lecture.
d: My parents assisted Professor Ruiz's lecture.
My relatives assisted Professor Ruiz's reading.
My parents attended Professor Ruiz's reading.
preguntas.x: Tíos y primos son relatives («parientes»); parents son solo el papá y la mamá. Ir a un evento es attend (assist = ayudar), y una charla o clase magistral es a lecture; reading es «lectura».

preguntas.q: Which sentence is correct?
preguntas.a: Remind me to tell Ana about the meeting, or I won't remember.
d: Remember me to tell Ana about the meeting, or I won't remind.
Remind me to say Ana about the meeting, or I won't remember.
Remember me to say Ana about the meeting, or I won't remind.
preguntas.x: Remind someone to do something es «recordarle a alguien que haga algo»; remember es acordarse uno mismo. Tell lleva la persona detrás (tell Ana), mientras que say no (say something to Ana).

preguntas.q: I ___ this novel from the library last week, so I have to return it by Friday.
preguntas.x: Borrow es «pedir prestado» (recibir): borrow something from someone. Lend es «prestar» (dar), con pasado lent, nunca lended; y rent es alquilar pagando.

preguntas.q: Come round to my flat on Saturday, and ___ your guitar with you!
preguntas.x: Bring es traer algo hacia donde está (o estará) quien habla: bring your guitar. Take es llevar en dirección contraria, fetch es ir a buscar algo y volver con ello, y carry on significa «continuar».

preguntas.q: The ___ by coach from London to Edinburgh was very ___; it took us almost ten hours.
preguntas.x: Un viaje concreto de un lugar a otro es a journey (o a trip); travel es incontable y se usa para viajar en general (Travel broadens the mind). «Largo» es long; large es un falso amigo que significa «grande».

preguntas.q: Which sentence is correct?
preguntas.a: Two men robbed a bank and stole £50,000.
d: Two men stole a bank and robbed £50,000.
Two men robbed a bank and robbed £50,000.
Two men stole a bank and stole £50,000.
preguntas.x: Se rob a una persona o un lugar (rob a bank, rob someone) y se steal lo que se llevan (steal money, steal a phone). Las demás oraciones usan uno de los dos verbos con el complemento equivocado.

preguntas.q: Which sentence means «Estudio la carrera de Derecho y quiero tener éxito»?
preguntas.a: I'm doing a law degree, and I want to be successful.
d: I'm doing a law career, and I want to have exit.
I'm doing a law degree, and I want to have exit.
I'm doing a law career, and I want to be successful.
preguntas.x: La carrera universitaria es a degree; career es la trayectoria profesional (a career in law). «Éxito» es success (be successful), y exit significa «salida».

preguntas.q: The government has decided to ___ the minimum wage by 5% next year.
preguntas.x: Raise es transitivo («subir algo»): raise prices, raise the wage. Rise es intransitivo (algo sube por sí mismo: Prices rise) y no lleva objeto, igual que arise («surgir») y rise up («sublevarse»).

preguntas.q: Which sentence is correct?
preguntas.a: Prices have risen sharply, and this has affected our sales.
d: Prices have raised sharply, and this has effected our sales.
Prices have risen sharply, and this has effected our sales.
Prices have raised sharply, and this has affected our sales.
preguntas.x: Rise – rose – risen es intransitivo (los precios suben solos), mientras que raise necesita objeto. Affect es el verbo «afectar»; effect es casi siempre sustantivo (have an effect on) y, como verbo, significa «llevar a cabo» (effect change).

preguntas.q: Which sentence means «Al principio el argumento de la novela me pareció confuso, pero al final lo entendí»?
preguntas.a: At first I found the plot of the novel confusing, but eventually I understood it.
d: At first I found the argument of the novel confusing, but eventually I understood it.
At first I found the plot of the novel confusing, but actually I understood it.
At first I found the argument of the novel confusing, but actually I understood it.
preguntas.x: El argumento de una historia es the plot; argument significa «discusión» o «razonamiento». Eventually sí significa «al final, finalmente», mientras que actually es «en realidad».

preguntas.q: Which sentence means «Pretendo realizar la encuesta y resumir los resultados»?
preguntas.a: I intend to carry out the survey and summarise the results.
d: I pretend to realise the survey and resume the results.
I intend to realise the survey and summarise the results.
I pretend to carry out the survey and resume the results.
preguntas.x: «Pretender» (tener la intención) es intend; pretend es «fingir». «Realizar» es carry out o do (realise es «darse cuenta»), y «resumir» es summarise; resume significa «reanudar».

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “Nobody was injured or killed in the fire.”
preguntas.a: There were no casualties in the fire.
d: The fire didn't happen by casualty.
Nobody was to blame for the fire.
Nothing was damaged in the fire.
preguntas.x: Casualties son las víctimas (heridos o muertos) de un accidente, un incendio o una guerra. Es un falso amigo: «casualidad» es chance o coincidence (by chance), y las otras opciones hablan de culpa o de daños materiales.

preguntas.q: Which sentence means «Mi tutora, que es muy simpática, me aconsejó comprar un carro más económico»?
preguntas.a: My tutor, who is very friendly, advised me to buy a more economical car.
d: My tutor, who is very sympathetic, adviced me to buy a more economic car.
My tutor, who is very friendly, adviced me to buy a more economical car.
My tutor, who is very sympathetic, advised me to buy a more economic car.
preguntas.x: «Simpático» es friendly o nice; sympathetic significa «comprensivo». El verbo es advise (advice es el sustantivo), y lo que gasta poco es economical; economic significa «de la economía» (economic growth).
